newsitem.title: CHILE: Guatemala to sign peace pact with rebels - Arzu.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala to sign peace pact with rebels - Arzu.

text.p: Guatemela will sign a peace agreement with leftist rebels on Dec. 29, ending 36 years of guerrilla war, President Alvaro Arzu said on Monday.

"We have just set the date for putting an end to 36 years of confrontation and that will be the signing of a peace agreement on Dec. 29," Arzu told an Ibero-American summit meeting in Chile. The surprise announcement drew loud applause from the leaders of 20 other countries at the summit.

The agreement, reached after five years of negotiations, will end Central America's sole remaining guerrilla war. More than 100,000 people, mostly civilians, have died in the fighting and an estimated 40,000 are missing.
Arzu did not immediately give details on the terms of the agreement. He and Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo embraced to thunderous applause after Arzu made the anouncement.

The summit attended by the leaders of 19 Latin American countries plus Spain and Portugal ended on Monday after three days of talks on strengthening democracy and widening citizen participation in politics in Latin America.

Guatemalan peace talks had stalled recently after a guerrilla commander was accused of kidnapping a woman, but the government and rebels resumed talks last weekend. At the time, Arzu said he was confident Guatemala would have a final peace agreement before the end of the year, as planned before the breakdown in negotiations.

The talks, which had been running smoothly for months, were abruptly suspended after rebel commander Rafael Valdizon was arrested on suspicion of kidnapping a member of an influential family that owns Guatemala's only cement company.
Valdizon was the second-in-command of one of the four rebel factions, but the guerrilla high command said he carried out the kidnapping without its knowledge.

Police briefly jailed him but let him go in return for freeing 86-year-old Olga Alvarado de Novella. After the government accused the guerrillas of violating terms of the negotiations and suspended talks, the rebels condemned the kidnapping and a few days later announced they would suspend propaganda exercises in Guatemala.
